paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's people don't get their way of living from the neighborhood they left or the one they're walking into. Before one single rule shows up, God says, "I am the LORD your God." (Lev 18:2) He says it again at the very end (Lev 18:30), so every rule sits between those two statements. Who He is comes first, and how they live comes after.

And look at the reason He gives for keeping His statutes and His judgments: "the man who does these things will live by them." (Lev 18:5) These aren't rules to make life smaller. They're given so His people can live. I've spent enough years stuck in the back of a drawer to know that what looks like a limit can be the very thing that keeps you from getting lost. Then God draws a hard line around a whole list of practices and calls them defiling, and that's a serious word. He says it applies to the native-born and to the foreigner living among them (Lev 18:26). I think this is one of the heavy parts, and it deserves a quiet moment.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Everybody around you is doing something, and the pull to just go along with it is REAL. God's call to His people is the same one it was here: He's the LORD your God, and you belong to Him, so you don't have to copy what's around you. Hold onto His Word, let it shape the way you live, and keep that apron on. There's more He wants to teach about what it looks like to be His.
